text: seekdb is an AI-native search database that unifies vector, full-text, structured, and semi-structured data in a single engine.
Hybrid search combines keyword matching with semantic vector similarity. seekdb performs both channels and fuses the results with reciprocal rank fusion.
A vector index such as HNSW supports approximate nearest neighbor search over dense embeddings, trading a little recall for large speedups.
A full-text index tokenizes documents and ranks them by term frequency, which helps when a query contains an exact keyword or a rare term.
Transformers.js runs ONNX models directly in the browser, so text embeddings can be computed on the user's device without any server call.
WebGPU gives the browser access to the GPU for model inference. When WebGPU is unavailable, a runtime can fall back to the CPU WebAssembly backend.
Quantizing an embedding model to INT8 reduces its file size and memory use, at the cost of a small drop in retrieval quality.
Half precision (FP16) stores weights in 16 bits, roughly halving model size compared with FP32 with negligible quality loss.
Reciprocal Rank Fusion merges several ranked lists by summing 1/(k + rank); it needs no score calibration across the channels being fused.
Retrieval augmented generation retrieves relevant passages first and then conditions a language model on them to produce grounded answers.
An embedding maps a piece of text to a dense vector so that semantically similar texts end up close under cosine distance.
The seekdb-js SDK exposes collections with full-text, dense vector, and sparse vector indexes, and a hybridSearch method for fused retrieval.
New documents become searchable after they are written and the index is refreshed, so incremental imports keep the knowledge base consistent.
Fetching keyword results and vector results separately and merging them in application code is not the same as a database-side hybrid query.
Cosine distance measures the angle between two vectors and ignores their magnitude, so normalization makes vector length irrelevant.
WebAssembly runs compiled code in the browser at near native speed and works on machines where the GPU is not available.
